newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. warns Japan will fall behind without open skies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns Japan will fall behind without open skies.

text.p: The United States warned Japan Thursday that it would be left behind in international aviation markets if it failed to consider U.S. "open skies" proposals.

Other Asian nations will soon begin negotiating open skies accords and it is in Japan's interest to join this movement, Alan Larson, assistant secretary of state for economic and business affairs, said.
"The world is moving in this direction. Countries that delay or resist risk being left behind," he said.
His statements came on the eve of "exploratory" talks in Tokyo between officials on whether to resume formal negotiations -- deadlocked since August -- in their long-running air services dispute.

The United States says its open skies proposal would mean the lifting of all government restrictions except for safety and security rules -- with resulting competition bringing increased air traffic and lower prices for consumers.
Japan, which believes that the current agreement signed in 1952 favours the United States, is wary.

"This (idea of) open skies will simply invite a domination of international markets by American mega-carriers," Jiro Hanyu, deputy general of the Transport Ministry's civil aviation bureau, told reporters last month.
"The present situation, under which Japan Airlines cannot fly to such cities as Detroit and Dallas ... must be corrected," he said.
The United States has already concluded open skies pacts with 12 European countries and with Jordan.
